rows.practice: designs and details buildings from first principles, producing accurate design information that meets regulation and integrates structure, fabric and services while managing hazards over the building life cycle
rows.knowledge: building technologies and materials and how they fit together, how building physics and pathology explain performance and the procurement routes and contracts that frame practice
rows.identity: an architectural technologist in training who conducts themselves ethically and professionally, guards health and safety and keeps current through reflection and development planning

rows.practice: leads innovative low-carbon design and retrofit through digital modelling and information management, diagnosing existing structures and steering collaborative decisions from concept to completion
rows.knowledge: how climate change and social, economic and political forces bear on building production and performance at every scale and how emerging technologies alter long-term upkeep
rows.identity: a responsible design professional who champions inclusive design and fair treatment, guards against unconscious bias and treats social justice as part of building well

rows.practice: frames a research problem, chooses and critically applies research methods and completes a major design or research project presented to academic and professional audiences
rows.knowledge: a critical, systematic grasp of sustainable design principles, emerging trends such as digital construction and how fabric, envelope and materials relate to climate, health and resources
rows.identity: an independent and original thinker in the built environment who weighs the professional and ethical stakes of design choices for sustainability and inclusion

distinctiveFeatures: An essential professional design discipline about how buildings are put together and perform (structure, systems, materials, fabric and services), rooted in science and engineering
The link between design and construction, optimising production and long-term performance across the building life cycle
Four educational components, theoretical, experiential, professional and ethical, tied to design, technology and practice; four main aspects, design, technology, management and practice
Shaped now by building and life safety law, the climate emergency, retrofit and data-driven, digital working such as BIM
Vocational and competency based: its standards are threshold only, and a lead PSRB, CIAT, accredits courses and confers the protected title
Inclusive design at its heart, with a record of widening participation

subjectSpecific.text: At master's level, you can make well-argued choices about what shapes sustainable and inclusive design.
At master's level, you can research and critically judge ways of designing a building's fabric and envelope, and show how they affect health and comfort inside.
At master's level, you can explain critically how more advanced technology, materials and services develop in relation to sustainability, inclusion and the wider community.
At master's level, you understand how the parts of sustainable design depend on each other and why theory meets limits in practice at different scales.
At master's level, you can examine critically how building methods and materials relate to the climate, the natural world and its resources.
At master's level, you show critical awareness of sustainable design principles and new technologies, drawing on many sources.
At master's level, you can critically weigh theories and judge how a sustainable design works spatially, visually, technically and socially in its wider setting.
At master's level, you can set objectives for a research problem in your field and choose and use established research methods to meet them.

transferable.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to carry out your share of the work in a team.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to pull together information and material from different sources.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to spot problems and work out the right questions to ask.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to analyse facts and data.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to see what is strong and what is weak in other people's arguments.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to sum up and draw together what is known about a topic.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to work on tasks on your own, with guidance when you need it.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to reflect on how you are progressing and act on the feedback you get.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to express yourself clearly, in speech and in other ways.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to present what you know, or an argument, so others can follow it.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to use the right digital systems to gather, analyse, choose and present information.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to give presentations using visuals and multimedia.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to show that you can grasp new ideas and information.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to show skill in recognising and describing what you are looking at.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to understand why health and safety, and equality, diversity and inclusion, matter at work.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to understand and join current debates on sustainability, careers and global perspectives, including decolonisation and anti-racism.
By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to see why acting sustainably matters and behave ethically.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.appliesTo: education and practice in the subject
statements.about: EDI embedded like health and safety; communicating the value of inclusive design
statements.paraphrase: Equality, diversity and inclusion should be built into education and practice as visibly as health and safety, since poorly designed buildings harm people and society; professionals in the field should be able to explain the worth of inclusive design in an accessible way.

forPractitioner.text: Build equality, diversity and inclusion into the curriculum as firmly as health and safety, and give students practice in explaining, accessibly, why inclusive design matters.

forBeneficiary.text: You should come to treat inclusion as seriously as safety in your design work, and be able to explain clearly to anyone why designing for everyone matters.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: UNESCO sustainability competencies aligned with outcomes
statements.paraphrase: The eight UNESCO competencies for sustainability should be matched to suitable learning outcomes in the curriculum, to change how staff and students think about and practise sustainable development.

forPractitioner.text: Map UNESCO's eight sustainability competencies (systems, futures, critical, strategic, collaborative, integrated problem-solving, self-awareness, normative) onto your module learning outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on curriculum design; the student meets its effect in their outcomes

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: integrated sustainability and real-life case studies
statements.paraphrase: Every course is meant to treat sustainability in a balanced, integrated and interdisciplinary way, so graduates know the goals they can serve; learners should work on real cases that build critical judgement of current and new solutions, and reflection.

forPractitioner.text: Thread sustainability through the whole course rather than one module, and use real case studies that make students judge existing and novel solutions and reflect on their choices.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design and teaching; the student meets it as case-study work

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: collaborative and enquiry-based learning
statements.paraphrase: Learners should be encouraged to share what they learn with peers and in their communities through collaborative learning, and be introduced to working with clients, contractors and suppliers; enquiry-based learning on real scenarios may also be used.

forPractitioner.text: Give students chances to share their learning with peers and beyond the classroom, bring in clients, contractors and suppliers, and consider enquiry-based projects set in real situations.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a teaching approach the course adopts; not a standard for the student to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.appliesTo: curricula and courses in the subject
statements.about: theory with practical projects; partnerships with industry
statements.paraphrase: Courses need both interdisciplinary and independent learning; new curricula should join theory to practical projects with sustainable design aims, and courses should build partnerships with industry, which grow confidence and employability.

forPractitioner.text: Pair interdisciplinary and independent work, join theory to practical projects with sustainable design aims, and build partnerships with industry so students apply theory in professional settings.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on curriculum design; the student meets it as projects and industry links

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: involving varied employers
statements.paraphrase: Providers should weigh the gains of involving employers of varied size and sector in several ways, including small groups on employer issues; corporate social responsibility drives much of that involvement, and employer views bring commercial realism to learning.

forPractitioner.text: Consider engaging employers of different sizes and sectors in light-touch ways, such as small working groups meeting online, and use their perspective to give learning commercial realism.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the institution in engaging employers

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: adaptability and specialisms in course design
statements.paraphrase: The statement sets general expectations and invites collaborative course design; since careers will be diverse and the industry will change, course design should foster adaptability, agility, diversity and specialisms to keep knowledge current.

forPractitioner.text: Use the statement as a starting point for shared course design, and build in room for adaptability, specialisms and new competencies so the course keeps pace with industry change.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: design, technology and practice in national and international context
statements.paraphrase: All degrees in the subject are expected to develop students' knowledge and critical understanding of design, technology and practice in national and international settings, and courses need an international dimension so graduates know the global context of their field.

forPractitioner.text: Students will build knowledge and critical understanding of design, technology and practice at home and abroad; include an international dimension so graduates understand where their profession works globally.

forBeneficiary.text: You will build knowledge and a critical understanding of design, technology and practice, both in the UK and internationally, and learn how your profession works across borders.

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: basic support services for students
statements.paraphrase: The support set out in 2.9 (screening, specialist help, mentors, reasonable adjustments, help with claims, accessible curricula) should be the minimum services for students, and the list is not complete.

forPractitioner.text: Treat screening for learning differences, specialist support, mentoring, reasonable adjustments, help with external claims and accessible curricula as the minimum support you offer.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the institution; the student meets it as support they can ask for

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: adjustments for presentation-based design assessment
statements.paraphrase: Adjustments suited to the subject's own assessments, such as presenting design work in person, should sit beside the usual exam adjustments; for students with learning differences or anxiety, presentations can build from one-to-one sessions to larger audiences over the year.

forPractitioner.text: Plan adjustments for design presentations as well as for exams: for example, let a student with anxiety start with one-to-one crits and build up to a full audience across the year.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on assessment design; a student may ask for the adjustment

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: digital poverty and individual circumstances
statements.paraphrase: Remote and blended learning widen access, but their use should always take account of each student's situation, with funding used to help those short of equipment, data or bandwidth.

forPractitioner.text: When moving teaching online or blended, check each student's access to equipment, data and bandwidth and use available funds to close the gaps.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the institution; the student meets it as support with equipment and data

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Architectural Technology degree

statements.about: a design project or dissertation with critical analysis of risks and ethics
statements.paraphrase: Students are expected to complete a design project, a dissertation or both, showing critical analysis, evaluation and reflection on the risks and ethical questions a proposed project raises.

forPractitioner.text: Students will complete a design project, a dissertation or both, in which they analyse, evaluate and reflect critically on the risks and ethics of a proposal.

forBeneficiary.text: You will complete a design project, a dissertation or both, in which you analyse and reflect critically on the risks and ethical questions your proposal raises.

statements.about: design, technology, management and practice in context
statements.paraphrase: All degrees in the subject are expected to develop knowledge and critical understanding of design, technology, management and practice in UK and international settings.

forPractitioner.text: Students will gain knowledge and critical understanding across all four aspects (design, technology, management, practice), set in UK and international contexts.

forBeneficiary.text: You will build knowledge and a critical understanding of design, technology, management and practice, in the UK and abroad.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: economical, sustainable processes and solutions from concept to completion
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to devise economical, environmentally sustainable, efficient processes and design solutions for complex design and construction problems, from concept to completion, to optimise how buildings are produced and perform.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course so students learn to produce economical, sustainable and efficient solutions to complex design and construction problems, carried from concept through to completion.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to create cost-effective, sustainable and efficient design solutions to complex building problems, from the first idea to the finished project.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: innovative design for the climate emergency
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to take innovative design approaches that answer the climate emergency and cut the effect of building on natural and built environments, reducing carbon emissions.

forPractitioner.text: Give students practice in innovative design that responds to the climate emergency and reduces carbon and environmental harm.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to use new design approaches that respond to the climate emergency and cut carbon emissions.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: graphical, written, digital and oral communication
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to build a wide range of communication skills, graphical and written, by hand and digitally, and to master oral presentation for any setting.

forPractitioner.text: Develop students' communication across drawing, writing, manual and digital media, and their spoken presentation to public and private audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you communicate well through drawings, writing and digital media, by hand and on screen, and present confidently to any audience.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: managing design and construction with digital technologies
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to manage design and construction by integrating architectural technology and digital tools, for new buildings and for retrofit.

forPractitioner.text: Teach students to manage the design and construction process using architectural technology and digital tools, on new-build and retrofit work.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to manage design and construction using digital tools, both for new buildings and for updating existing ones.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: responding to wider context, including climate change
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to respond quickly and intelligently to social, economic, environmental, technical, cultural and political contexts, climate change included, at every scale from local to international.

forPractitioner.text: Help students read and respond to the wider setting of a project (its social, cultural, economic, political, technical and environmental sides), climate change included, from local to global.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to respond thoughtfully to the wider context of a project, from local to global, including climate change.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: accurate design information that meets standards
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to work systematically in producing accurate design information that meets standards and law, integrating envelope and interior with structure, fabric and services.

forPractitioner.text: Teach a systematic method for producing accurate design information that complies with standards and law and coordinates envelope, interior, structure, fabric and services.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to produce accurate design information that meets standards and the law, fitting the outside, inside, structure and services together.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: managing the building life cycle with information systems
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn strategies that use information management systems to run the building life cycle well, for safety and use.

forPractitioner.text: Give students strategies for using information management systems to manage a building across its life cycle, for safety and use.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to use information systems to manage a building well across its whole life, for safety and everyday use.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: new concepts, technologies and practices
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to take up new concepts, technologies and practices that affect long-term production, performance and upkeep of buildings, new and existing.

forPractitioner.text: Prepare students to adopt new concepts, technologies and practices that bear over time on how buildings are produced, how they perform and how they are maintained.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you take up new ideas, technologies and practices that affect how buildings are made, perform and are maintained over time.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: diagnosing existing structures
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to assess existing structures through building diagnostics and pathology so that solutions suit the existing structure, fabric and services.

forPractitioner.text: Teach building diagnostics and pathology so students can assess existing structures and make proposals that fit them.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to diagnose the condition of existing buildings so that your designs suit what is already there.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: health and safety from first principles to occupation
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to build health and safety practice in from first principles through occupation and maintenance, fire and life safety and legislation among them.

forPractitioner.text: Teach students to embed health and safety, including fire and life safety and the law, from first design principles through occupation and maintenance.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should teach you to build health and safety, including fire and life safety, into your designs from the start through to how the building is used and maintained.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: business and management skills for practice
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to build business and management skills, covering industry and professional standards, client engagement, procurement and work with other professionals, service providers and authorities.

forPractitioner.text: Develop students' business and management skills: professional and industry standards, clients, procurement and working with other professionals and authorities.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you build business and management skills, from working with clients and other professionals to how projects are procured.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: promoting equality, diversity and inclusion
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to take up and champion equality, diversity and inclusion so that people are treated fairly and given fair chances.

forPractitioner.text: Help students adopt and champion equality, diversity and inclusion so that treatment and opportunity are fair.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you champion equality, diversity and inclusion, so that people are treated fairly and get fair chances.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: respecting difference and preventing unconscious bias
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to recognise and value difference, make settings where all feel welcome and valued whatever their identity, and understand and guard against unconscious bias.

forPractitioner.text: Help students value difference, build welcoming settings for people of every identity, and understand and counter unconscious bias.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you value people's differences, make everyone feel welcome whoever they are, and notice and guard against your own unconscious bias.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology honours degrees

statements.about: ethical, professional and responsible conduct
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students learn to act ethically, professionally and responsibly, aware of social justice and ethics and working collaboratively and communicating well.

forPractitioner.text: Help students conduct themselves ethically, professionally and responsibly, aware of social justice, working collaboratively and communicating effectively.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you act ethically, professionally and responsibly, with an eye to social justice, working well with others and communicating clearly.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: critically informed choices for sustainable, inclusive design
statements.paraphrase: Make choices grounded in critical thought about the factors that shape the delivery of sustainable and inclusive design.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates make critically grounded choices on the factors shaping sustainable and inclusive design.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you can make well-argued choices about what shapes sustainable and inclusive design.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: appraising fabric and envelope methods for healthy buildings
statements.paraphrase: Research, analyse and critically judge design methods for building fabric and envelope, and find how they bear on a healthy, comfortable indoor environment.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates investigate and critically judge design methods for fabric and envelope and trace their effect on health and comfort indoors.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you can research and critically judge ways of designing a building's fabric and envelope, and show how they affect health and comfort inside.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: articulating advanced technology linked to sustainability and inclusion
statements.paraphrase: Explain, with critical judgement, the growth of more complex technology, construction, materials and services tied to sustainability and to advances in the built environment and community, inclusive design among them.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates explain critically the development of more complex technology, construction, materials and services in relation to sustainability, inclusive design and wider community advances.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you can explain critically how more advanced technology, materials and services develop in relation to sustainability, inclusion and the wider community.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: complexity and constraints of sustainable design
statements.paraphrase: Gain critical awareness of how the parts of sustainable design depend on one another and of the limits met when theory is put into practice at different scales.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates understand critically how sustainable design's parts interlock and the constraints on applying its theory at scales from building to district.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you understand how the parts of sustainable design depend on each other and why theory meets limits in practice at different scales.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: technology, construction and materials in relation to climate and resources
statements.paraphrase: Examine critically how architectural technology relates design and construction methods, materials and components to climate, the natural world and resources.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates examine critically how the discipline links construction methods, materials and components to climate, nature and resources.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you can examine critically how building methods and materials relate to the climate, the natural world and its resources.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: sustainable design principles and emerging technologies
statements.paraphrase: Show critical awareness of the principles of sustainable design and of new technologies and ideas, drawing on many kinds of source.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates show critical awareness of sustainable design principles and emerging technologies, drawn from a wide range of sources.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you show critical awareness of sustainable design principles and new technologies, drawing on many sources.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: judging theory and the qualities of sustainable design at scale
statements.paraphrase: Evaluate theoretical approaches critically and reach reasoned judgements on how a sustainable design works in space, appearance, technique and society at the scale of wider development.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates evaluate theories critically and judge the spatial, aesthetic, technical and social qualities of sustainable design in its wider setting.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you can critically weigh theories and judge how a sustainable design works spatially, visually, technically and socially in its wider setting.

headingPath: Structure and aims of Architectural Technology master's degrees

statements.about: research objectives and methods
statements.paraphrase: Set objectives for a chosen research problem in the subject, then judge critically and use established research techniques to meet them.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates set research objectives for their problem and critically choose and apply established research techniques to pursue them.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you can set objectives for a research problem in your field and choose and use established research methods to meet them.

statements.about: professional, ethical and practical issues at master's level
statements.paraphrase: Master's students will deepen their subject while weighing its professional, ethical and practical questions.

forPractitioner.text: Master's students will extend their command of the subject and weigh its professional, ethical and practical questions as they do so.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you will take your subject further while weighing the professional, ethical and practical questions it raises.

statements.about: an advanced research or design project, communicated professionally
statements.paraphrase: Master's students will strengthen their research skills through an advanced research or design project, thinking critically and creatively, framing questions, designing a method and producing original knowledge, and will present the work to academic or professional audiences in writing, speech and visuals.

forPractitioner.text: Master's students will complete an advanced research or design project with their own questions and method, aiming at original knowledge, and will present it professionally in written, spoken and visual forms.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you will carry out an advanced research or design project with your own questions and methods, aim to add something new to the field, and present it professionally in writing, in person and visually.

statements.about: an explicit assessment strategy
statements.paraphrase: Courses should have a clear assessment strategy in their design that follows the learning outcomes, supports learning, lets students show rising attainment and matches the teaching methods used.

forPractitioner.text: Write an explicit assessment strategy into the course design, tied to the outcomes and the teaching methods, that lets students show progress level by level.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

statements.about: an accessible mix of assessment methods
statements.paraphrase: Assessment in the subject should use a mix of methods that, taken together, students from different educational and cultural backgrounds can access.

forPractitioner.text: Use a varied mix of assessment methods so that, across the course, students from different educational and cultural backgrounds are not shut out.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on assessment design

statements.about: adjustments discussed with the student
statements.paraphrase: Where a method of assessment may disadvantage a student, adjustments must be considered together with that student, keeping the whole cohort fairly treated.

forPractitioner.text: If an assessment method could disadvantage a student, you must discuss possible adjustments with them, while keeping things fair for the rest of the cohort.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student takes part in the discussion it requires

statements.about: a range of assessment methods matched to outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Courses should use varied assessment methods that match the variety of their learning outcomes; the ten methods listed after it are an indication of practice, not a checklist.

forPractitioner.text: Match the variety of assessment methods to the variety of learning outcomes; the listed methods (design projects, exams, reports, presentations, portfolios and others) show current practice, not a required set.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

statements.about: Annex D for performance above threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do far better than threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows this and should refer to the degree classification descriptions in Annex D for FHEQ Level 6 and FQHEIS Level 10.

forPractitioner.text: When setting marking criteria above the pass, refer to Annex D's descriptions of the four honours classifications rather than to this statement, which stops at threshold.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in setting classification criteria

statements.about: fluency in design, technology, management and practice
statements.paraphrase: All courses are expected to make students fluent in the four main aspects of the subject: design, technology, management and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Students will become fluent in the four main aspects of the subject (design, technology, management, practice); the standards are met by showing understanding of these and applying them.

forBeneficiary.text: You will become at home in the four main parts of the subject: design, technology, management and practice.

statements.about: the wider factors shaping the discipline
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows grasp of the wider forces (social, economic, environmental, political, legal, ethical and technical) acting on the discipline and its practice at local, regional and global scale.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates understand the social, economic, environmental, political, legal, ethical and technical forces on the discipline, from local to global.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you understand the social, economic, environmental, political, legal, ethical and technical forces on your field, locally and globally.

statements.about: professional conduct, practice, design leadership, procurement and contracts
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows grasp of professional conduct and ethics, how practice works, design leadership and management roles (such as lead or principal designer, design and information management), procurement routes and contract administration.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates know professional conduct and ethics, practice, design leadership and management roles, procurement and contract administration.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you know how to behave professionally and ethically, how practice runs, what design leaders and managers do, and how projects are procured and contracts run.

statements.about: building technologies and how elements interrelate
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows grasp of building technologies and how elements, systems, components, materials and methods fit together across building types, in new construction and adaptation, and serve the building's functions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates know construction technologies and how elements, systems, components and materials interact across building types and serve their function.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you understand how building parts, systems and materials fit together in different kinds of building and what each does.

statements.about: design principles, building science and values for new and existing buildings
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows grasp of architectural and technical design principles, building science (the basics of building physics and pathology) and the values guiding work on new and existing buildings, such as conservation, renovation and adaptation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates understand design principles, the basics of building physics and pathology, and the values behind work on new and existing buildings.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you understand design principles, the basic science of how buildings behave and decay, and what guides work on old and new buildings.

statements.about: holistic design and detailing from first principles
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows the ability to design as a whole and detail from first principles for production, performance and sustainability, responding to regulation, health and safety, wellbeing and new sustainable technologies.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates design holistically and detail from first principles for production, performance and sustainability, meeting regulation, safety and wellbeing.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you can design a building as a whole and work out its details from first principles, so it can be built, performs well and is sustainable, safe and healthy.

statements.about: client, user and stakeholder needs and project scope
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows the ability to work with client, user and stakeholder needs, analysing a development and reading its context to set a fitting project scope.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates analyse client, user and stakeholder needs and the setting of a development to define its scope.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you can work out what clients, users and others need, analyse the proposal and its setting, and decide what the project should cover.

statements.about: health and safety, hazards and risk over the life cycle
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows the ability to work within regulatory health and safety requirements, finding, analysing and judging hazards and risks when designing, to secure health, safety, welfare and security over a building's life, compliance and enforcement included.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates apply regulatory health and safety requirements, assessing hazards and risks in design for safety and security across the building life cycle.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you can spot and assess hazards and risks in your designs and keep people safe and secure throughout a building's life, within the law.

statements.about: resilient, sustainable, inclusive solutions
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows the ability to produce design solutions that are resilient, sustainable and inclusive, both as complete systems and in detail, for varied situations, informed by current thinking and by climate change.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates create resilient, sustainable and inclusive solutions, whole and detailed, informed by current knowledge and climate change.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you can create designs that are resilient, sustainable and inclusive, both as a whole and in detail, with climate change in mind.

statements.about: modelling and information management in collaborative work
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows grasp of current approaches, processes and technologies for modelling, communicating and managing information, and applies them in collaborative work to support decisions driven by data.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates understand and apply current methods and tools for modelling and managing information in collaboration, for data-driven decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you understand and use current tools for modelling and sharing information in a team, so decisions rest on data.

statements.about: staying current through reflection and development planning
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the graduate shows awareness of current and new topics, technologies and practices, regulations and standards included, kept up through reflecting on oneself, naming development needs and planning action, so as to stay current and to specialise.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates track current and emerging topics, technology, regulation and standards, and use reflection and development planning to stay current and specialise.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your honours degree, you will show that you keep up with new topics, technologies, rules and standards by reflecting on your own needs and planning how to develop.

statements.about: critical awareness of context and underpinning theories
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the master's graduate shows critical awareness of the past and present context and of the social, economic, environmental, political, legal, ethical and technical theories shaping practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, master's graduates show critical awareness of historical and current context and of the theories behind practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your master's degree, you will show critical awareness of your field's history and present context and of the theories that shape its practice.

statements.about: current and emerging trends such as digital construction
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the master's graduate shows systematic understanding and critical awareness of present and emerging trends, digital construction among them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, master's graduates understand systematically and critically the current and emerging trends in the field, such as digital construction.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your master's degree, you will show a systematic, critical understanding of current and emerging trends in your field, such as digital construction.

statements.about: evaluating methods for complex problems
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the master's graduate shows the ability to weigh up suitable methods for handling complex problems.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, master's graduates evaluate which methods suit complex problems.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your master's degree, you will show that you can weigh up which methods suit complex problems.

statements.about: independent analysis with some originality
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the master's graduate shows independent analysis of complex ideas, used to drive critical discussion, with some originality.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, master's graduates analyse complex concepts independently and bring some originality to critical discussion.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your master's degree, you will show that you can analyse complex ideas on your own and add something original to critical debate.

statements.about: a major design work or substantial research project
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, the master's graduate has completed a major design work or a substantial research project grounded in a thorough grasp of the discipline.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, master's graduates complete a major design or substantial research project based on thorough disciplinary understanding.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for your master's degree, you will complete a major design or research project that rests on a thorough understanding of your field.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: teamwork on assigned tasks
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to carry out the tasks given to them within a team.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to complete the tasks they are given as team members.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to carry out your share of the work in a team.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: combining information from several sources
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to gather information and material from varied sources into one whole.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to combine information and material from several sources.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to pull together information and material from different sources.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: identifying problems and questions
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to spot problems and the questions they raise.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to identify problems and frame questions.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to spot problems and work out the right questions to ask.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: analysing factual information
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to analyse information of a factual kind.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to analyse factual information.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to analyse facts and data.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: judging others' arguments
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to see where the arguments of other people are strong and where weak.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to judge the strengths and weaknesses of others' arguments.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to see what is strong and what is weak in other people's arguments.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: synthesising what is known on a topic
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to draw together what is currently known about a given subject or topic.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to synthesise the current state of knowledge on a topic.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to sum up and draw together what is known about a topic.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: working independently with guidance
statements.paraphrase: Should be able, with guidance, to carry out tasks on their own.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to work on tasks independently, with guidance available.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to work on tasks on your own, with guidance when you need it.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: reflection and using feedback
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to review their own progress and act on the feedback given.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to reflect on their progress and use feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to reflect on how you are progressing and act on the feedback you get.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: communicating verbally and non-verbally
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to communicate well in speech, in other forms, or both.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to communicate effectively verbally, non-verbally or both.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to express yourself clearly, in speech and in other ways.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: presenting so others understand
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to set out knowledge or an argument so other people can follow it.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to present knowledge or an argument clearly to others.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to present what you know, or an argument, so others can follow it.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: digital information handling
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to use suitable digital systems to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to gather, analyse, choose and present information with suitable digital systems.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to use the right digital systems to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: presentations with visual aids and media
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to give presentations supported by visual aids and media.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to deliver presentations using visual aids and multimedia.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to give presentations using visuals and multimedia.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: grasping new ideas and information
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to show they can grasp new ideas or information when met.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to show they understand new ideas or information.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to show that you can grasp new ideas and information.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: recognising and describing material
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to show skill in identifying and describing material.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to show skill in recognising and describing material.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to show skill in recognising and describing what you are looking at.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: health and safety and EDI at work
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to understand why health and safety, and equality, diversity and inclusion, matter at work.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to explain why health and safety, and equality, diversity and inclusion, matter in the workplace.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to understand why health and safety, and equality, diversity and inclusion, matter at work.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: current debates on sustainability, employability and global perspectives
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to value and take part in current debates on sustainability, employability and global outlooks, decolonisation and anti-racism included.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to appreciate and join current debates on sustainability, on employability and on global outlooks, decolonisation and anti-racism among them.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to understand and join current debates on sustainability, careers and global perspectives, including decolonisation and anti-racism.

headingPath: Generic skills for Architectural Technology graduates

statements.about: acting sustainably and ethically
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to see the need to act sustainably and to behave and conduct themselves ethically.

forPractitioner.text: Honours graduates should be able to appreciate the need for sustainable action and show ethical behaviour.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your honours degree, you should be able to see why acting sustainably matters and behave ethically.
